title: Read File
summary: Read the text file at `path` and return its lines, each trimmed, without blank lines and without comment lines (lines whose first non-blank character is `#`). Accept both `\n` and `\r\n` line endings. If the file can't be read, fail with an error whose message includes the path, so the reader knows which file it was.

files.todo.txt:
# shopping

buy milk
   # remember the receipt
  call the bank

hints: Every language has a one-call way to read a whole text file into a string. Look up how yours reports a file that isn't there: an error value, an exception, or `nil` plus a message.
Split the text on `\n`, then trim each line: trimming also removes the `\r` that Windows line endings leave behind. Skip empty lines and lines that start with `#` after trimming.
Some languages' read errors don't mention the path (Rust's `io::Error` doesn't). Add it yourself, the way you added the key in error-context: put the path in front of the original message.

cases.description: reads a last line without a newline
an empty file has no lines
a file of blank lines has no lines
a missing file is an error that names it
